newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 2.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 2.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Thursday:

* President Suharto said on Tuesday Indonesia's economy was expected to grow by around 7.8 percent in 1996, compared with 8.2 percent in 1995, while inflation was expected to be around 6.7 percent, against 8.6 percent in 1995.
* The Dow Jones industrial average fell 101.10 points to 6,448.27 on Tuesday, leaving it up 26 percent for the year after a rise of 33.5 percent in 1995.
* Indonesia said it expected to earn $6 billion from foreign tourists in 1996, an increase of 18 percent from the previous year.
* President Suharto pledged on Tuesday that his government would push for openness and democracy in 1997.
* Indonesia, plagued by cement shortages in past years, is projected to see an oversupply of over two million tonnes in 1997.

* The Jakarta Composite Index rose 4.94 points, or 0.78 percent, to close at 637.43 points last Friday as late session window-dressing pushed prices higher at the close of the last trading day of the year.
* On Thursday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,361.25/61.75 in early trading against the opening of 2,362.25/63.25.
* Alumindo Light Metal Industry on its debut on the Jakarta stock exchange today.
* Cement manufacturers Semen Cibinong, Indocement and Semen Gresik on reports of a possible oversupply in 1997.

* Bank Bira on reports a subsidiary of General Electric Co of the United States had bought a seven percent stake in the bank, and that it expected to post a net profit of 60 billion rupiah in 1996 against 30.34 billion rupiah last year.
* Chicken restaurant franchiser Putra Sejahtera Pioneerindo on market talk that a foreign investor was interested in buying a stake in the firm.
